trial_name: MR CLEAN — A Randomized Trial of Intraarterial Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke
citation: Berkhemer OA, Fransen PSS, Beumer D, et al; MR CLEAN Investigators. A randomized trial of intraarterial treatment for acute ischemic stroke. N Engl J Med. 2015;372:11-20.
one_liner: Intraarterial treatment (predominantly mechanical thrombectomy) within 6 hours of anterior-circulation LVO stroke improved 90-day disability outcomes and functional independence compared with usual care alone.

pico.population: Adults with acute ischemic stroke due to proximal anterior-circulation occlusion (ICA, M1, M2, A1–A2) confirmed by CTA/MRA/angiography, within 6 hours of symptom onset
pico.intervention: Intraarterial treatment (arterial catheterisation with mechanical thrombectomy, intra-arterial thrombolytic therapy, or both) added to usual care
pico.comparison: Usual care alone (including IV alteplase when eligible)
pico.outcome: 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ordinal shift analysis

background.existing_knowledge: Proximal anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion (LVO) causes a large proportion of disabling strokes and has poor natural history without early reperfusion. Intravenous alteplase achieves low early recanalisation rates in proximal LVO. Earlier endovascular strategies and several pre-2015 RCTs were limited by delayed workflows, variable imaging confirmation of occlusion, and limited use of modern stent-retrievers. By the early 2010s, stent-retrievers and better imaging/workflow created biological plausibility for benefit.
background.knowledge_gap: Definitive pragmatic RCT evidence for intraarterial treatment in routine care settings was lacking.
background.hypothesis: In adults with acute ischaemic stroke due to proximal anterior-circulation occlusion treatable within 6 hours, intraarterial treatment added to usual care would shift the full modified Rankin Scale (mRS) distribution towards less disability at 90 days.

methods.design: Randomised, multicentre (16 centres), investigator-initiated, pragmatic superiority trial; open-label treatment with blinded endpoint assessment (PROBE design).
methods.setting: Acute stroke care in the Netherlands; enrolment required vessel imaging confirmation of proximal anterior-circulation occlusion.

inclusion: Proximal anterior-circulation occlusion (ICA terminus/M1/M2/A1–A2) on CTA/MRA/angiography
Eligibility for intraarterial treatment within 6 hours of symptom onset
exclusion: Standard contraindications to IV thrombolysis (when considered), including persistent blood pressure >185/110 mmHg despite treatment
Other protocol-defined exclusions (e.g., clinical/imaging features precluding endovascular therapy)

methods.intervention: Intraarterial treatment (arterial catheterisation with mechanical thrombectomy, intra-arterial thrombolytic therapy, or both) in addition to usual care. Initiation within 6 hours of symptom onset. Among those receiving intervention, retrievable stents used in 81.5%, additional intra-arterial thrombolytics in 10.3%, acute carotid artery stenting in 12.9%, general anaesthesia in 37.8%.
methods.comparison: Usual care alone, including IV alteplase when eligible and other standard acute stroke management; no protocolised endovascular rescue outside trial allocation.
methods.blinding: Open-label delivery of endovascular therapy; functional outcomes (including primary outcome mRS at 90 days) assessed by personnel blinded to treatment assignment.
methods.sample_size_power: 500 patients to provide 82% power (β=0.18) at α=0.05 to detect a 10% absolute increase in the cumulative proportion of patients with mRS 0–3 at 90 days, assuming 10% cross-over.
methods.primary_outcome: Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 90 days, analysed by ordinal logistic regression (shift analysis).
secondary_outcomes: New ischaemic stroke in different vascular territory

headline_bullets: Disability improved across the full mRS distribution (adjusted common OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.21–2.30).
Functional independence (mRS 0–2) increased from 19.1% to 32.6% (adjusted OR 2.16, 95% CI 1.39–3.38).
Mechanistic endpoints showed strong recanalization (75.4% vs 32.9% no occlusion on follow-up CTA) and smaller infarct volumes.
Procedural harms included higher rates of any intracranial haemorrhage (29.2% vs 18.4%) and new-territory strokes (5.6% vs 0.4%).

outcomes_table.outcome: No intracranial occlusion on follow-up CTA

outcomes_table.note: Smaller infarct volume in intervention group; incomplete data

outcomes_table.outcome: New ischaemic stroke in different vascular territory

subgroup_table.note: Point estimate suggests retained benefit in severe stroke

safety: New ischaemic stroke in different vascular territory: 5.6% vs 0.4% (RR 14.91, P<0.001)
Death within 30 days: 18.9% vs 18.4% (RR 1.03, P=0.88); no significant difference at 7, 30, or 90 days

domains.notes: Central web-based randomisation; stratified for centre, baseline NIHSS, planned IV alteplase use, and planned endovascular modality. Group sizes imbalanced (233 vs 267) but baseline characteristics broadly similar; key imbalances favoured control group.

Open-label treatment; co-interventions and post-procedure care could differ. Primary outcome assessment blinded, reducing detection bias for mRS; many secondary outcomes were objective but had incomplete ascertainment.
502 randomised, 2 withdrew consent immediately excluded, 500 analysed. Minor deviation from strict ITT, numerically trivial. Primary endpoint ascertainment at 90 days effectively complete.

Intraarterial treatment initiated in 84.1% of intervention arm; 15.9% did not receive it (no occlusion at angiography, clinical improvement, access failure, etc.). Crossover low (3.6%). Device/technique heterogeneity (81.5% retrievable stents, 10.3% IA thrombolytics, 12.9% carotid stenting).

Age, NIHSS, onset-to-randomisation comparable. High alteplase exposure in both arms (87.1% vs 90.6%). Occlusion distribution typical of proximal LVO. Some imbalances (left-hemisphere strokes, alteplase use) favoured control.

internal_validity.verdict: Overall, internal validity is strong to moderate: randomisation and blinded endpoint assessment support causal inference, and objective mechanistic endpoints demonstrate separation; key limitations are open-label care, incomplete delivery of intraarterial therapy in 15.9% of the intervention arm, and incomplete imaging ascertainment for some secondary outcomes.

domains.notes: Broad pragmatic enrolment (age 23–96, median NIHSS 17–18) and high alteplase uptake reflect routine early-window LVO care in a mature stroke system with vascular imaging for triage.

Most generalisable to anterior-circulation proximal LVO within 6 hours in well-resourced systems with rapid imaging, transfer, and 24/7 endovascular capability. Less applicable to posterior circulation, distal occlusions, very late/unknown onset, and settings without such access. Technique and workflow have evolved since MR CLEAN, so absolute outcomes may differ.

external_validity.verdict: Generalisability is good for early-window anterior LVO in well-resourced stroke systems, but limited in settings lacking rapid vascular imaging/endovascular access or in patient groups outside the trial’s anatomic and temporal eligibility.

strengths: First large pragmatic multicentre RCT demonstrating clear functional benefit of an intraarterial strategy for confirmed proximal anterior-circulation occlusion.
Clinically meaningful primary endpoint (mRS shift) with blinded assessment; high follow-up completeness for primary outcome.
Mechanistic coherence: marked improvement in vessel patency on follow-up CTA and reduced infarct volume.
High background rate of alteplase use supports “add-on” interpretation (thrombectomy on top of modern medical therapy).
limitations: Open-label treatment introduces potential performance bias in supportive care and rehabilitation intensity (mitigated by blinded mRS assessment).
Incomplete protocol delivery: 15.9% of the intervention arm did not receive intraarterial therapy; reperfusion rate (mTICI 2b/3) was 58.7%—lower than in later-generation practice.
Device/technique and anaesthesia heterogeneity complicate attribution to any single procedural approach and may increase between-centre variability.
Important procedural harm signal: more new-territory infarcts (5.6% vs 0.4%) and higher “any intracranial haemorrhage” (29.2% vs 18.4%).

critical_appraisal.summary: A well-designed, pragmatic trial with clear, consistent benefit across multiple outcomes, despite some limitations in blinding and incomplete treatment delivery. External validity is high for early-window LVO in similar settings.
strengths: Randomised, stratified, with blinded primary endpoint assessment
Strong mechanistic separation on imaging and clinical scales
High external validity for the target population
weaknesses: Moderate reperfusion rates by current standards

sections.authors_conclusion: MR CLEAN establishes intraarterial treatment (predominantly mechanical thrombectomy) as an effective strategy to improve disability outcomes in early-window anterior-circulation LVO when added to best medical therapy.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: Intraarterial treatment (mechanical thrombectomy) should be offered to eligible patients with acute anterior-circulation LVO within 6 hours of symptom onset, as it improves functional outcomes.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Adults with proximal anterior-circulation occlusion (ICA, M1, M2, A1–A2) confirmed by vascular imaging, within 6 hours, and with no contraindications.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: It does not mean that all patients benefit equally; the benefit is substantial but requires rapid systems of care and expertise. It does not eliminate the need for IV alteplase in eligible patients.
implementation_caveats: Rapid imaging and transfer systems are essential
Procedural expertise is needed to minimise new-territory strokes

controversies.topic: Why MR CLEAN succeeded when earlier endovascular RCTs were neutral
controversies.notes: Key differentiator: mandatory vessel imaging confirmation of proximal occlusion before randomisation, aligning the intervention with the biological target population. Contemporary devices and techniques were used frequently (retrievable stents 81.5%), despite overall reperfusion rates being modest compared with later trials.
The accompanying editorial emphasised that benefit depends on rapid workflow and experienced centres, and framed MR CLEAN as the beginning of a new era requiring disciplined systems of care.

New-territory infarction occurred more often with intraarterial treatment (5.6% vs 0.4%; RR 14.91), underscoring that net benefit requires procedural expertise and attention to embolic protection/technique. Symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage was similar (7.7% vs 6.4%), supporting acceptable haemorrhagic risk in an alteplase-rich population.

controversies.topic: Rapid confirmatory RCTs and end of equipoise
controversies.notes: Multiple 2015 trials in similar populations (e.g., ESCAPE) corroborated improved functional outcomes with thrombectomy, accelerating guideline adoption. Patient-level meta-analysis (HERMES) confirmed consistent benefit across a broad range of ages and severity.
Later trials using advanced imaging selection expanded thrombectomy benefit into later time windows (DAWN, DEFUSE 3), reshaping triage and transfer paradigms for late-presenting LVO.
Major stroke guidelines incorporated thrombectomy for eligible anterior-circulation LVO and emphasised speed and imaging-based selection (AHA/ASA 2018 guideline and 2019 update).

context_related_trials.relation: Another 2015 trial that confirmed functional benefit of thrombectomy for anterior-circulation LVO, reinforcing MR CLEAN's findings.
Later trial expanding thrombectomy benefit into later time windows (6–24 hours) using advanced imaging selection.
Trial showing benefit of thrombectomy in 6–16 hour window with perfusion imaging selection.
Patient-level meta-analysis of multiple thrombectomy trials (including MR CLEAN) confirming consistent benefit across a broad range of ages and severity.

unresolved_questions: Optimal anaesthetic strategy during thrombectomy (general anaesthesia vs conscious sedation)
Effect of faster door-to-reperfusion times on outcomes
Benefit in posterior circulation or distal occlusions
Long-term functional and quality-of-life outcomes beyond 90 days

numbers_to_remember: Primary mRS shift adjusted common OR 1.67 (95% CI 1.21–2.30)
quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: For early-window anterior-circulation LVO, intraarterial thrombectomy improves 90-day functional outcomes and should be standard of care.
